documents.title: Emergency Department Physician Note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED. DOS 03/18/2025. Copy to PCP 03/28/2025.

20M, college student. Meningococcal meningitis 08/2024 (this hospital); also allergic rhinitis and acne. Roommate brought him in after spotting a rash on his arms and legs. Got home from a spring break trip two days ago; felt achy and run-down, which he put down to travel, then over the past few hours spiked a high fever with severe headache and could not bend his neck. Disoriented in triage, history limited, partly from roommate.
Meds: cetirizine PRN, adapalene gel. Allergies: NKDA. Never smoker; drinks socially, more on the recent trip per roommate.

T 39.2 C, BP 90/60, P 120, RR 22.
Petechiae with patches of purpura on the extremities. Nuchal rigidity, Brudzinski positive. Cap refill 3 s.

Labs: WBC 15.0, plt 100. Na 130, K 4.5, BUN 18, Cr 1.2. CRP 24 mg/L. Blood cultures sent, pending.
LP: CSF WBC 2000 with 90% PMNs, protein 150, glucose 20.

Impression: acute bacterial meningitis with meningococcemia; thrombocytopenia.
IV fluids. Ceftriaxone 2 g IV in the ED. Droplet precautions. Admitted to medicine.

documents.title: Call From Patient's Mother
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Mother called early, upset. Gavin's roommate took him to the ED last night with fever, headache, a stiff neck and a rash; he was confused when he got there. Admitted again on IV antibiotics. Family drove over overnight. She asks whether this is the same thing as last summer; told her I don't know yet and the hospital team will know more once the tests are back. Asked her to keep us posted and that I'd see him after discharge. Requested ED and inpatient records.

documents.title: Out of the hospital again
documents.author: patient
documents.body: got discharged yesterday. was in about 8 days. they said my platelets were low at first but came back up before I left. no meds to take home. I'm at my parents' for a few days

documents.title: RE: Out of the hospital again
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for letting me know, and I'm sorry you went through that again. Let's see you in about 10 days with a blood count. Front desk will text you a time. Same warning signs as before: fever, headache, rash, confusion, call or text right away, day or night.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Post-Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen after his second meningitis admission.

ED 3/18, two days after coming back from a spring break trip: fever, headache, stiff neck, rash with purpura, low BP, confused. ED note (received 3/28): WBC 15, platelets 100, Na 130, Cr 1.2, CRP 24; CSF WBC 2000, 90% PMNs, protein 150, glucose 20; blood cultures pending at the time. Treated as bacterial meningitis with meningococcemia. He says about 8 days inpatient on IV antibiotics, platelets recovered before discharge on 3/26, nothing to take home. No discharge summary or culture result has come to us.

Now: back in classes this week, tired by evening but improving. No headache, fever or neck pain. Rash faded over the first week home. Hearing fine. Thinking clearly, catching up on coursework.
Meds: cetirizine PRN, adapalene. NKDA.
Social: drank more than usual on the spring break trip, back to weekends only.

Exam: well-appearing. Afebrile, BP normal. Skin: no petechiae, purpura or scarring on the arms or legs. Neck supple. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Alert and oriented, cranial nerves intact, strength and gait normal.

A/P
1. Acute bacterial meningitis with meningococcemia and thrombocytopenia, recovered. CBC and BMP today to make sure platelets, sodium and creatinine are back to normal.
2. Allergy season coming: start cetirizine daily.
3. Acne: continue adapalene.
Physical in July.

documents.title: Your Labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good news: platelets, white count and hemoglobin are all normal, and so are your sodium and kidney function. Nothing more to check for now.

documents.title: Missed Physical
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Called about yesterday's missed 9:00 physical. He apologized, had the date wrong. Rebooked for Tuesday 7/29 at 8:20. Reminder text set for the day before.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Physical, rescheduled from 7/8.

Since April: feels back to normal, finished the semester. No fevers, headaches or rashes. Allergies were manageable on daily cetirizine in spring. Skin okay on adapalene.
History: meningitis admissions 8/2024 and 3/2025, recovered from both.
Meds: cetirizine PRN, adapalene 0.1% nightly. NKDA.
Social: dorm again in the fall. Alcohol on weekends; he volunteers that the spring break trip was the heaviest drinking he has done and that it scared him a little after what followed. No tobacco or vaping.

PHQ-2 0. AUDIT-C 3.

Exam: vitals fine. HEENT normal. Neck supple, no nodes. Heart RRR, lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Skin: occasional comedones, no lesions on the extremities. Neuro normal.

A/P
- Healthy 20 y/o, recovered from two meningitis admissions.
- Tdap today; last one at 11 per pediatric record.
- Alcohol: under the screening cutoff; talked through pacing and keeping an eye on friends.
- Rhinitis and acne stable on current regimen.
- Flu shot in the fall.

documents.title: Nurse Visit: Flu Vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu vaccine, trivalent, 0.5 mL IM right deltoid. Feels well. Declined COVID this year, says he'll think about it. Tolerated, observed 15 min.
